name: Redtape Ltd
title: Redtape Ltd - 543957 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Q4 FY26 EBITDA 19.4% and FY26 revenue INR2,415 crore (+19.6%), but inventory still ~170 days, payables fell sharply and management was evasive on payables, margins and apparel economics.

summary.headline: RedTape FY26 revenue rose 19.6% to INR2,415 crores and EBITDA margin widened to 19% from 17.5%, with standalone PAT of INR244 crores.
summary.overview: Management described FY26 as a year where the business absorbed a weak first half and then accelerated in Q3 and Q4, helped by the GST cut on footwear below INR2,500. Q4 revenue was INR674 crores with a 43.4% gross margin and standalone PAT of INR71 crores. Management attributed the lower reported gross margin to e-commerce rebates now netted against top-line, with other income carrying these rebates. Working capital improved: debt fell about INR200 crores from September to March and operating cash flow was stated at INR175 crores, though inventory days remain high at about 170.

segments.name: Footwear
segments.commentary: INR1,535 crores in FY26, about 63% of revenue; remains the footfall anchor, with casual and athleisure growing within it.

segments.name: Apparel
segments.commentary: INR805 crores in FY26, about 34% of revenue; management is investing most here for FY27, including women's apparel. Segment margin not disclosed.

segments.name: Accessories
segments.commentary: INR75 crores in FY26, about 3% of revenue; sunglasses, hard luggage and grooming grew faster than the other segments from a small base.

segments.name: Brands
segments.commentary: Ozark (outdoor/adventure) response exceeded expectations and store rollout is being scaled. Bond Street and Mode were launched in FY26; no figures given.

guidance_outlook: Plan to open 200-250 stores in FY27 (500-1,500 sq ft), with COCO share of 25-35% and the rest FOFO; expansion into South and West India.
Inventory target of 150 days, described as 'very near future'; management earlier said it could settle at 120-150 days.
EBITDA margin band guided at 16-19%, described as a 'new normal' rather than a peak.
No MRP increase planned for the next 3-6 months; raw-material cost volatility to be reassessed after September.
Long-term target of 65-70% of revenue from retail (offline); no multi-year revenue target given.
capex_capacity: Store count crossed 550 (223 exclusive showrooms across 161 cities at year-end per prepared remarks); about 70% of stores in North India, present in 300 cities.
Seven marketplace warehouses in India, with plans to open two more; Ludhiana warehouse opened in FY26.
Unnao warehouse expanded by about 3 lakh sq ft; remaining capex went to retail expansion. Management referenced about INR450 crores of prior capex without a FY26 breakdown.
Store economics: in the franchise (FOFO) model, the franchisee bears rent, salaries, miscellaneous costs and fixtures capex; RedTape keeps billing and top line.
demand_pricing: Channel mix: offline retail about 70% of turnover; online (e-commerce and quick commerce) about 30%, primarily via Flipkart and Myntra on a marketplace model.
Management cites RedTape as the number two footwear brand on Flipkart and Myntra; online repeat customers at 54-58%.
Pricing: no MRP hikes yet; company works on cost-plus and has about six months of POs and LCs covered.
Management said the Q4 volume lift was not only GST-driven, citing wedding season, healthy footfalls and same-store growth; SSSG was 17.8% in Q4.
Tier 2 and Tier 3 towns hold the majority of stores; consumer shift to organised branded product cited.

qa_highlights.question: Why is inventory high (about 175 days on sales, over 300 days on COGS) and where will it settle?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said inventory peaked above 250 days and is now about 170, driven by marketplace warehouse build-out and offline expansion. The target is 120-150 days, with 150 as the ideal near-term level.

qa_highlights.question: Why did gross margin fall while EBITDA improved, and what is the medium-term EBITDA view?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said e-commerce rebates are now netted against revenue, so the gross margin decline is top-line driven, with no PBT impact. CFO said EBITDA has hovered around 16-18%, with 19% described as a new normal.

qa_highlights.question: What is the other income of INR133 crores and the FY25 restatement?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said about INR88 crores is e-commerce discounts/rebates and the rest is claims from platforms. The FY25 restatement was an accounting change, applied to the prior year as well.

qa_highlights.question: What is the apparel margin and the operating cash flow outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management does not report footwear and apparel margins separately and did not give a figure. On cash flow, CFO said operating cash flow reached INR175 crores and debt fell about INR200 crores since September.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Pre-Ind AS EBITDA margin, the COCO/FOFO split, and the accessories strategy?
qa_highlights.answer: Pre-Ind AS EBITDA margin is about 16.4%. About 25-27% of stores are COCO. Accessories expansion is framed as raising wallet share and SSSG, building on belts, wallets and caps.

qa_highlights.question: Payable days appear to have dropped sharply; what is driving this?
qa_highlights.answer: Management initially deferred the question and the CFO said he would revert, citing payable days history of about 171-188 days in recent years.

risks_watch: Inventory at about 170 days versus the 150-day target; operating cash flow and short-term borrowings depend on this.
Payable days reportedly fell sharply (about 55 days per an analyst's reading); management has not yet explained this.
Raw material cost pressure; price increases are deferred until after September, and no price hikes are taken.
Gross margin optics shaped by e-commerce rebate accounting; EBITDA margin band is wide (16-19%).
Apparel margin not disclosed, and the segment is now 34% of revenue and the focus of FY27 investment.
Store expansion of 200-250 outlets in FY27 must clear return thresholds from day one, per management.
summary.management_tone: Confident on FY26 results and brand momentum, but guarded on specifics: management deferred several questions (payable days, apparel margin, footwear vs apparel split) and gave no multi-year revenue target.
key_quotes: What comes through clearly is that the business has held its shape through all of that and then accelerated.
It is not the store count that we are chasing. Every location we open has to clear our return thresholds from day one.
We are pleased to announce that the Board has recommended a final INR2 per equity share on the face value of INR2.
We are the number two footwear brand on Flipkart and Myntra.

adds.what: 200-250 new stores in FY27 (500-1,500 sq ft), COCO 25-35% and rest FOFO, expanding into South and West India
Two additional marketplace warehouses in India (seven existing)

growth.why: Management plans 200-250 store additions in FY27 with 6 months of POs and LCs covered and SSSG of 17.8% in Q4, but no FY27 revenue growth number was given and store-level revenue or capex was not quantified, so backing is partial.
